title: Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging of Molecular Rotors in Living Cells
protocol: Prepare a stock solution of the dye by dissolving approximately 1 mg/ml of the dye in an appropriate solvent.
Grow cells on a multiwell plate with a coverslide underside for microscopy in an incubator at 37 °C with a 5 % CO2 atmosphere until ~80% confluent.
Add 10 - 20 μl of the stock solution to the living cells growing in a multi-well plate containing 4 ml of Opti-MEM medium per well for a 6-well plate.
Return the multiwell plate to an incubator at 37 °C with a 5 % CO2 atmosphere for 10-45 mins for staining.
Remove the multiwell plate from the incubator and wash the cells 3-4 times with 4 ml optically clear cell culture medium to remove excess dye.
Transfer the multiwell plate to the microscope stage and connect to a temperature controller / 5 % CO2 gas inlet as required, in preparation for imaging.
Place the sample on the microscope stage.
Obtain a transmission image to identify fluorescent cells.
Obtain a fluorescence image to identify fluorescent cells.
Verify that the fluorescence emanates from expected locations (e.g., cell membrane, cytoplasm).
Obtain a fluorescence emission spectrum and verify it matches the dye or protein expected (spectrum of the molecular rotor).
Image a non-stained sample as a negative control and verify it does not fluoresce.
Switch to FLIM mode by moving a mirror out of the fluorescence detection beam path.
Insert an appropriate fluorescence emission filter to block any exciting light from reaching the detector.
Scan the sample.
Check that the detector count rate (CFD) on the acquisition control software is no more than about 1% of the laser repetition rate (SYNC).
If the detector count rate exceeds 1%, reduce the laser excitation intensity by placing a neutral density filter in the laser beam path.
Acquire a FLIM image for typically 3-5 minutes.
Stop scanning and save the raw data as a 3D data cube consisting of spatial coordinates x and y, and time.
Open the raw data in fluorescence decay analysis software such as TRI-214 or commercial software.
Display the fluorescence intensity image, which is the integrated fluorescence decay in each pixel.
Inspect the fluorescence decay in a selected pixel.
If the peak count is below 100, use spatial binning of pixels.
Add counts of adjacent pixels into the central pixel.
Alternatively, repeat the measurement for a longer acquisition time.
Select a global pixel threshold value above which decays are fitted.
Apply a single exponential decay fit to the image.
Encode the fluorescence lifetime in color for each pixel above the threshold.
Check the reduced chi-squared values for various pixels.
Inspect the corresponding residuals, which should be randomly distributed around zero.
Adjust the colour range such that the fluorescence lifetime distribution fits into the colour range.

If a monoexponential fit does not yield a chi-squared value of around 1 (and up to 1.3), and there is a systematic deviation of the residuals from zero, try fitting a double exponential model to the fluorescence decays.
Fit a double exponential model to account for two different environments the probe may be in.
Use the fit to obtain pre-exponential factors or amplitudes indicating relative amounts of dye in one environment or the other.
Alternatively, use a stretched exponential function to account for a distribution of fluorescence lifetimes.
Encode results for fluorescence lifetimes, pre-exponential factors, and lifetime ratio and pre-exponential factor ratio for each pixel in color.
Colour each pixel according to its value to obtain contrast due to fluorescence lifetimes, pre-exponential factors and their ratios.
Check the reduced chi-squared values (which can also be encoded in colour and displayed as an image) - around 1 (and up to 1.3) indicates a good fit.
Inspect residuals, which should be randomly distributed around zero.
Incubate living cells with the fluorescent molecular rotor.
Observe a punctate dye distribution in the fluorescence images.
Capture FLIM images of HeLa cells incubated with a meso-substituted BODIPY dye.
Fit the fluorescence decays in every pixel using a single exponential decay model.
Plot the lifetimes extracted from every pixel to obtain a fluorescence lifetime histogram.
